audit.whatIsWrong: The page says Null Sphere silences Renekton and calls it 'the only thing that can interrupt your combo', and it attributes the magic shield to Kassadin's passive.
audit.why: Riot's text for Null Sphere: it deals damage and interrupts channels, and the excess energy forms a shield that absorbs MAGIC damage. There is no silence in the description — the kit file's 'channel' flag is a tooltip-parsing misfire off the words 'interrupting channels', and the mirror flagged the same thing. Renekton has no channels: E, W and Q cannot be interrupted by it, and every point of Renekton's damage is physical, so the shield absorbs none of it. Kassadin's passive (Void Stone) is magic damage reduction and ignoring unit collision. On top of that, a 50-Fury Ruthless Predator destroys damage shields on the target, so the Null Sphere shield is deleted rather than absorbed through, and it stuns 1.5s. Kassadin's own burst opens with Nether Blade, an auto-attack reset — the wind-up is the tell, not the cast.
audit.corrected: The silence claim is removed from early, mid, whys[4], spikes[1] and both wants[] entries; the shield is correctly attributed to Null Sphere and stated as magic-only and shield-strippable; Nether Blade's auto reset is added as the trade tell in whys[0] and early.

edits.before: Pre-6 this is your lane to dictate. Kassadin's Q silence is the only thing that can interrupt your combo — bait it by stepping up empty-handed, wait for the cast, then immediately E-in and drop empowered W before the silence can stop you. At Level 1 he wins if he auto-harasses you out of melee range, so build Fury on the wave before committing. At Level 2 you spike harder than almost anyone in the game: E-in, 50-Fury W-stun, Q-heal, E-out erases 40% of his HP and he has nothing to dash away with. By Level 3, your goal is a health lead large enough that he cannot risk standing at the wave without Riftwalk up.
edits.after: Pre-6 this is your lane to dictate. Null Sphere interrupts channels only — it cannot stop your E, W or Q, so nothing he owns breaks your combo; his one real out is walking, and Nether Blade's auto-reset wind-up is your cue to step back. At Level 1 he wins if he auto-harasses you out of melee range, so build Fury on the wave before committing. At Level 2 you spike harder than almost anyone in the game: E-in, 50-Fury W-stun, Q-heal, E-out erases 40% of his HP and he has nothing to dash away with. By Level 3, your goal is a health lead large enough that he cannot risk standing at the wave without Riftwalk up.

edits.before: Level 6 makes this genuinely even. His Riftwalk lets him blink out of your second-E escape or follow-up your dive from an unexpected angle, and his passive shield absorbs a chunk of your empowered W burst. Do not commit a full all-in if Riftwalk is up — bait it with a fake E step, let him blink away or toward you, then run your pattern the instant it is on cooldown. Dominus gives you the HP and Fury generation to survive one Riftwalk reposition and still finish the trade, but if you stall until he has two Riftwalk blinks available you lose the exchange.
